# Introduction

This vignette demonstrates a full RNA-seq to pathway-visualization workflow using `supervisoR`. The example uses a publicly available kidney-biopsy RNA-seq dataset from diabetic kidney disease patients (`GSE142025`) together with `DESeq2` for differential expression and `piano` for pathway analysis.

The goal is not to prescribe a single upstream analysis strategy. Instead, the vignette shows one reproducible way to produce a pathway-by-condition score matrix that can be visualized with `supervisoR`.

```{r setup}
library(supervisoR)
library(DESeq2)
library(dplyr)
library(magrittr)
library(readr)
library(tibble)
library(piano)
library(tidyr)
```

# Load expression data from GEO

The code below is adapted from the GEO2R workflow (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/geo2r) and simplified for direct use in R.

```{r}
urld <- "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/download/?format=file&type=rnaseq_counts"
path <- paste(
  urld,
  "acc=GSE142025",
  "file=GSE142025_raw_counts_GRCh38.p13_NCBI.tsv.gz",
  sep = "&"
)

tbl <- as.matrix(read_tsv(path)) %>%
  `rownames<-`(.[, 1]) %>%
  .[, -1]

apath <- paste(
  urld,
  "type=rnaseq_counts",
  "file=Human.GRCh38.p13.annot.tsv.gz",
  sep = "&"
)
annot <- read_tsv(apath, quote = "")
rownames(annot) <- annot$GeneID
```

# Define groups and build a DESeq2 dataset

```{r}
gsms <- "000000000000000000000111111222222222"
sml <- strsplit(gsms, split = "")[[1]]

gs <- factor(sml)
groups <- make.names(c("aDKD", "eDKD", "Healthy"))
levels(gs) <- groups
sample_info <- data.frame(Group = gs, row.names = colnames(tbl))

keep <- rowSums(tbl >= 10) >= min(table(gs))
tbl <- tbl[keep, ]

ds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = tbl,
  colData = sample_info,
  design = ~ Group
)

ds <- DESeq(ds, test = "LRT", reduced = ~ 1)
```

# Extract gene-level statistics

Here we calculate log2 fold changes for each disease group relative to healthy controls and then collapse duplicated gene symbols by averaging the numeric columns.

```{r}
r_aDKD <- results(
  ds,
  contrast = c("Group", "aDKD", "Healthy"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  pAdjustMethod = "BH"
) %>% as.data.frame()

r_eDKD <- results(
  ds,
  contrast = c("Group", "eDKD", "Healthy"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  pAdjustMethod = "BH"
) %>% as.data.frame()

r_all <- left_join(
  r_aDKD %>%
    rownames_to_column("gene") %>%
    dplyr::select(gene, log2FoldChange),
  r_eDKD %>%
    rownames_to_column("gene") %>%
    dplyr::select(gene, log2FoldChange),
  by = "gene",
  suffix = c(".aDKD", ".eDKD")
) %>%
  left_join(
    .,
    annot %>%
      as.data.frame() %>%
      dplyr::select(GeneID, Symbol) %>%
      mutate_all(as.character),
    by = c("gene" = "GeneID")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(!gene) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Symbol) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(across(where(is.numeric), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  column_to_rownames("Symbol") %>%
  `colnames<-`(sub("log2FoldChange\\.", "", colnames(.)))
```
# Run pathway analysis

In this example we use the Reactome hierarchy included with `supervisoR`, then run `piano` with `fgsea` as the pathway statistic engine.

```{r}
default_data <- load_default_data(
  database = "reactome",
  species = "Homo sapiens"
)

myGSC <- piano::loadGSC(stack(default_data$gene_sets))
res_list <- list()

set.seed(42)
for (i in colnames(r_all)) {
  tmp_lfc <- r_all[i] %>%
    mutate_all(~ replace_na(.x, 1))

  piano_res <- piano::runGSA(
    geneLevelStats = tmp_lfc,
    gsc = myGSC,
    geneSetStat = "fgsea",
    signifMethod = "geneSampling",
    nPerm = 10000,
    adjMethod = "BH",
    gsSizeLim = c(5, Inf)
  )

  tmp_res <- piano::GSAsummaryTable(piano_res) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      Name,
      `Stat (dist.dir)`,
      `p adj (dist.dir.up)`,
      `p adj (dist.dir.dn)`
    ) %>%
    `colnames<-`(c(
      "pathway",
      "statDistinctDir",
      "pAdjDistinctDirUp",
      "pAdjDistinctDirDn"
    )) %>%
    mutate(contrast = i) %>%
    mutate_at(
      vars(pAdjDistinctDirUp, pAdjDistinctDirDn),
      ~ if_else(is.na(.), 1, .)
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      direction = case_when(
        pAdjDistinctDirUp > pAdjDistinctDirDn ~ "up",
        pAdjDistinctDirUp < pAdjDistinctDirDn ~ "down",
        TRUE ~ "neither"
      )
    )

  res_list[[i]] <- tmp_res
}

pw_out <- do.call(rbind, unname(res_list)) %>%
  dplyr::select(pathway, statDistinctDir, contrast) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = pathway,
    names_from = contrast,
    values_from = statDistinctDir
  ) %>%
  column_to_rownames("pathway")
```

# Visualize a pathway family

Now that we have a pathway-by-condition matrix, we can visualize any branch of the Reactome hierarchy.

```{r}
lollipop_colors <- c(
  aDKD = "#CC6677",
  eDKD = "#332288"
)

p1 <- plot_subgraph(
  parent_geneset_name = "Metabolism Of Lipids",
  mapping = default_data$mapping,
  g = default_data$pathway_graph,
  gene_sets = default_data$gene_sets,
  pathway_column = NULL,
  enrichment_scores = pw_out,
  conditions = colnames(pw_out),
  layout = "kk",
  hide_nodes_without_enrichment = TRUE,
  use_node_label = TRUE,
  repel_labels = FALSE,
  max_depth = 1,
  lollipop_plot = TRUE,
  lollipop_colors = lollipop_colors,
  glyph_size = c(180, 130),
  lollipop_size_scale = 0.65
)

print(p1)
```

# Explore the full hierarchy interactively

When you want to browse many top-level pathway families before focusing on a specific one, the Shiny app is the easiest entry point.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
run_pathway_shiny_app(
  mapping = default_data$mapping,
  g = default_data$pathway_graph,
  gene_sets = default_data$gene_sets,
  pathway_column = NULL,
  enrichment_scores = pw_out,
  conditions = colnames(pw_out),
  glyph_size = c(80, 60),
  res = 96,
  hide_nodes_without_enrichment = TRUE,
  lollipop_plot = TRUE,
  lollipop_colors = lollipop_colors,
  layout_options_plot = list(
    layout = "layout_with_kk",
    physics = FALSE,
    smooth = FALSE,
    type = "full",
    randomSeed = 42,
    options = NULL
  )
)
```

# Summary

The essential requirement for `supervisoR` is a pathway-by-condition matrix aligned to a hierarchy. In this vignette the matrix came from RNA-seq differential expression followed by pathway analysis, but the same visualization workflow applies to other pathway scoring approaches as long as the output is a signed pathway-level score per condition.
